# Should I Use Chicago Title?
> Independent first-person commentary by a Chicago Title Insurance Company policyholder. Not the website of Chicago Title or Fidelity National Financial.

## Account and evidence
- [Chicago Title insurance review](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/): Policyholder reports a boundary dispute, removal of three boards, at least $80,000 in defense expenses so far in an ongoing boundary case, and approximately $2 million in title insurance. These are the policyholder’s statements; original policy and coverage letter are not published.
- [Claim narrative](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#experience): The policyholder’s account of the initial refusal to defend and subsequent refusal of incurred costs for lack of advance approval.
- [Fidelity ownership](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#fidelity): Sourced ultimate-parent relationship to Fidelity National Financial. Avoidance recommendation is the policyholder’s opinion.
- [Court decisions](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#other-cases): Bartel (2025) and Fifth Third (2012) adverse bad-faith rulings; Lindeman (2026) denial of summary judgment, not a liability finding. Each decision has a source link and qualifications.
- [Questions and answers](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#quick-answers): Short answers with links to the underlying account or external sources.
- [About this account](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#record): Authorship, privacy, approximation and source limitations.

- [What I am doing about it](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#what-im-doing): The owner states an intention to sue Chicago Title and publish public filings and publishable correspondence as the case develops. No filings from that case are posted yet.

- [Share your experience](https://shouldiusechicagotitle.com/#share-your-experience): Contact the site owner at ken@shouldiusechicagotitle.com to discuss similar experiences and the possibility of exploring a class action with an attorney. This is an invitation, not an announcement of a filed or certified class action.

## Document status
Prepared and updated October 29, 2026. No court determination about the website owner’s claim is reported. No company-wide frequency or misconduct finding is claimed. Later proceedings in linked cases have not been comprehensively checked.

Claim clarification: Chicago Title acknowledged that the boundary was in dispute. The policyholder says the company refused to address related trespass and damages claims despite their connection to the boundary. This is not a statement that the insurer acknowledged ownership of the boards’ location.
